title: CMake: Remove the wireshark_nsis_prep target
description:
The code signing step is done during installer compilation. A
separate prep target to sign the NSIS uninstaller is no longer
necessary, since 9195d634.

Remove the CMake wireshark_nsis_prep target. Adjust the documentation
and CI builds.

TODO: Test portable apps NSIS build.

notes.body: @geraldcombs Can you confirm this will not adversely affect the `Windows x64 Package` CI job or other requirements around code singing I may not be aware of?

The main thing is to ensure that the packaging targets don't somehow rebuild our binaries and clobber any code signatures. IIRC this was an issue in the past (mabye when we were still using Nmake?) and the "prep" targets were added in order to establish a clear demarcation between building our package dependencies and the packages themselves. They probably aren't needed nowadays.
I see. Maybe we should keep it then.

commits_data.title: CMake: Remove the wireshark_nsis_prep target
commits_data.message:
CMake: Remove the wireshark_nsis_prep target

The code signing step is done during installer compilation. A
separate prep target to sign the NSIS uninstaller is no longer
necessary, since 9195d6348278524da7e4d20c9ca0f24bc826e2e2.

Remove the CMake wireshark_nsis_prep target. Adjust the documentation
and CI builds.

commits_data.title: CMake: Cleanup some options
commits_data.message:
CMake: Cleanup some options

Try to be smarter about setting ENABLE_SIGNED_NSIS.

Instead of skipping the whole Qt deployment, including things like
translations, just skip the DLLs in the manifest. This is useful
if the target machine has Qt installed and the static DLL list
for cross-compiling is not adequate.
